main_text.l: C fit rectus, 2. erigatur quadratum super latus trianguli
quod recto angulo opponitur, vt hoc loco super linea
B D ereximus quadratum B K L D, 3. erigantur duo
alia quadrata super duabus aliis lineis siue lateribus eius-
dem trianguli, vt quidem hoc loco ereximus quadratū
super linea B C E F, super linea vero C D quadratum
Dico quod quadratum B K L D sit æquale duobus re-
liquis quadratis in hac figura depictis,
nempe quadrato B C E F & quadrato C D G H.
quadrati latus idem attingat siue secet in puncto K.
deinde connectantur etiam duo anguli nempe B & H per li-
neam B H item duo anguli ad D & ad E per lineam, E D.
His igitur hypothesibus siue postulatis concessis sic pro-
cedet demonstratio. Quoniam duo anguli nempe, D C
B. & D C G sunt anguli recti, idcirco & lineæ, G C & C B
istos angulos includentes erunt lineæ ductæ, in dire-
ctum, id est, fiet ex istis duabus lineis vna recta, idq; per
propositionem 14. lib. 1. quæ per seipsam facile intelligi-
tur. Iam quia anguli C. D. H. & B. D. L. æquales sunt cum
sint recti, si addatur communis angulus C D B. vtique
totus angulus B D H æqualis erit toti angulo C. D. M
per axioma natura notum: Si æqualibus æqualia Si quis

page.notes: Diagram of a square-based figure with labelled points (E, F, C, D, G, H, B, K, L, M, A, N) and interior lines; the labels are rendered as shown. Lower part of the page is cut off; the final word "æqualia" is continued on the next part. Several letters in the diagram are partly illegible and are not transcribed. The text is cut off at the left edge of the scan, so the first letters of many lines are missing; the visible words are transcribed as far as they can be read. Some words at the line starts are incomplete and have been left as far as legible. The line "Si quis hanc" has the initial letters partly lost.
